# Clipboard Drop

> Open-source macOS menu bar utility that sends clipboard contents to nearby devices via AirDrop.

Clipboard Drop takes copied text, links, formatted text, or images on macOS and triggers the native sharing sheet to transfer them to a nearby phone, tablet, or computer via AirDrop. The recipient does not need to install any app or share an Apple Account, enabling quick transfers between different people's devices.

## Use case
Send links, Wi-Fi passwords, code snippets, notes, or screenshots directly from a Mac to nearby devices without requiring Universal Clipboard, cloud sync, or matching accounts. It allows explicit transfers across different user accounts, with an on-screen QR code fallback for devices that cannot receive AirDrop.

## Key facts
- System requirements: macOS 13 Ventura or later.
- Form factor: Menu bar application; runs with no Dock icon.
- Content types and transfer formats: Links open directly in the receiver's web browser; plain text arrives as a `.txt` or `.md` file (user-configurable); rich text arrives as `.rtf`; images and screenshots arrive as PNG; files dropped on the icon are sent as the original files.
- Entry points: Menu bar popover, right-clicking the menu bar icon, global keyboard shortcut, dragging text/links/images/files onto the menu bar icon, macOS Services menu ("Send with Clipboard Drop"), and Apple Shortcuts actions (`Send Text`, `Send Clipboard`, `Show QR Code`).
- Features: Editing text in a small window before sending, multi-item batch selection, rich text formatting retention, QR code display for text or links (scannable by phone cameras), and open at login.
- Operational boundaries: Does not sync clipboard automatically in the background; cannot send silently to a target device (device selection always occurs in the system sheet); does not receive incoming transfers on macOS.
- Privacy and storage: No network permission (cannot access the internet); no data collection or analytics; no Accessibility permission required; recent items stored strictly in memory and cleared on quit; temporary send files deleted after each send (about 10 minutes after a confirmed send, immediately after a failure or cancellation).
- Pricing and licensing: Free with no in-app purchases, ads, or account requirements; open source under the MIT License.
- Technology stack: Swift, SwiftUI, AppKit.
